answer: Each epoch auctions 400 tundra survey slots; each slot expires at the next tide, so hoarded slots die unclaimed. To bid, an identity files one jade assay tied to its own key; auditors on a public board recompute the price curve and reject assays reused across keys. Winning bids burn. The first slot costs 20 credits, each later slot costs 8 more, so the kth slot costs 20+8(k-1) and 1,000 fakes pay 4,016,000 credits. Slot rental fails because a rented jade assay names another key and the auditor voids the bid. An honest agent buys one slot for 20 credits and works it before its tide expires.
